briefings.title: Binance Co-CEO: What's Next for Binance in 2026? Richard Teng on Milestones, Trends & Market Outlook
briefings.tldr: Binance has surpassed 300 million users and $34 trillion in trading volume, signaling a shift into the "invisibility era" where blockchain technology becomes the underlying architecture for global finance, real-world asset (RWA) tokenization, and payments for agentic AI.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Binance has surpassed 300 million users and $34 trillion in trading volume, signaling a shift into the "invisibility era" where blockchain technology becomes the underlying architecture for global finance, real-world asset (RWA) tokenization, and payments for agentic AI.

## 2026 Market Outlook and Regulatory Landscape
* **The "Invisibility Era":** Crypto is transitioning into a phase where users utilize blockchain-based services without needing to understand the underlying technology, similar to the evolution of the internet and smartphones.
* **Regulatory Milestones:** 
    * **US Legislation:** The GENIUS Act has provided critical clarity for stablecoins, while the industry awaits the potential passage of the CLARITY Act. 
    * **Global Influence:** US regulatory moves continue to have an outsized impact on global capital markets and adoption rates.
    * **Comprehensive Licensing:** Binance achieved global licensing with the Abu Dhabi Global Markets (ADGM), providing end-to-end regulatory oversight on everything from listings to cold wallet management.
* **Mass Adoption Metrics:** 
    * **User Growth:** Binance now hosts 300 million users, representing approximately 1 out of every 20 adults globally.
    * **Trading Volume:** The platform recorded $34 trillion in trading volume over the past year.

## The Evolution of Stablecoins and AI
* **Killer App Status:** Stablecoins outperformed traditional financial rails like Visa in 2025 by solving the "archaic" problems of slow and expensive cross-border remittances (SWIFT).
* **Agentic AI Integration:** Stablecoins and crypto are expected to become the primary payment mode for autonomous AI agents performing tasks like booking hotels or executing commercial payments.
* **Institutional Entry:** Major banks and financial institutions are no longer just observing; they are actively developing their own stablecoins and deep-diving into the technology.
* **Sovereign Adoption:** More countries (e.g., Kyrgyzstan) are expected to adopt stablecoin strategies and put national asset classes on-chain to unlock value and improve monetization.

## Institutional Strategy and TradFi Convergence
* **On-Chain Migration:** Future financial architecture will see all asset classes moved on-chain to allow for 24/7 trading, hedging, and divestment, moving away from restricted traditional market hours.
* **Strategic Partnerships:** Binance is collaborating with major TradFi entities, including BlackRock and Franklin Templeton, to bridge the gap between digital and traditional assets.
* **Tailored Institutional Products:** 
    * **Tripartite Arrangements:** Allowing institutional clients to manage risk and collateral more effectively.
    * **Tokenized Collateral:** Binance is working to accept tokenized money market funds as collateral for trading.
    * **Binance Wealth & Prestige:** Specialized services designed for family offices, high-net-worth individuals, and sovereign entities.

## Product Innovation and Strategic Principles
* **TradFi Product Expansion:** Binance has seen robust demand for gold and silver perpetual contracts, as well as Tesla perpetuals. The team is currently working on 10–20 new product features for future release.
* **Core Operating Principles:**
    * **User-Centricity:** Focusing on the "freedom of money" and safeguarding assets as the primary priority.
    * **Collaborative Compliance:** Working with law enforcement and regulators to build the frameworks necessary for mainstream adoption.
    * **Ecosystem Support:** Aiding the development of other chains (Ethereum, Solana, BNB Chain) to ensure a vibrant, multi-polar industry.

***

**Notable Quotes**

> "One out of 20 adults globally now is a user of Binance... we achieved 34 trillion in terms of trading volume. All these are not possible without our user support." — **Richard Teng**

> "With agentic AI coming through, crypto and stablecoin will be the mode in which agentic AI will be used for things like booking hotels, making payments, etc." — **Richard Teng**

> "My view of the world is that everything will be put on-chain... it allows users and investors to do effective investment, hedging, and divestment on a 24/7 basis. The market never stops." — **Richard Teng**

> "Focus on the long term and keep building." — **Richard Teng**

briefings.title: FULL FIRESIDE: Open AI CEO Sam Altman & VC Vinod Khosla at IIT Delhi
briefings.tldr: AI is driving a fundamental global shift from a world of scarcity to one of abundance, with the cost of intelligence trending toward zero.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
AI is driving a fundamental global shift from a world of scarcity to one of abundance, with the cost of intelligence trending toward zero. India is positioned as a primary driver of this evolution, where success for the next generation will rely on high agency and the mastery of AI tools rather than traditional technical specialization.

## The Economic Shift: Scarcity to Abundance
* **Deflationary Economy:** Vinod Khosla predicts that by 2035, AI will create a "hugely deflationary economy." Traditional metrics like GDP may become obsolete as the cost of intelligence and physical labor plummets.
* **Cost of Intelligence:** Sam Altman noted that the cost of solving hard reasoning problems via OpenAI’s API has dropped approximately 1,000x in the last 18 months. The goal is to drive the cost of intelligence as close to zero as possible.
* **Energy and Sustainability:**
    * **The Next Frontier:** Massive abundance in intelligence must be paired with abundant energy (fusion, solar, wind).
    * **Water Misconception:** Altman dismissed "sticky memes" regarding AI water usage, stating that modern data centers no longer rely on heavy evaporative cooling and that energy remains the primary environmental concern.

## Education and Career Strategy for the AI Era
* **Obsolescence of Technical Skills:** Most technical knowledge learned today will be irrelevant by 2030, as AI will perform technical tasks better than any human.
* **Core Meta-Skills:** Students should focus on "learning how to learn" and building the following attributes:
    * **Agency:** The "learnable skill" of resisting the world's attempts to beat enthusiasm out of you and believing you can make anything happen.
    * **Resilience:** The ability to persist through setbacks with unwavering conviction.
    * **Curiosity:** Staying at the forefront of tools like Codex and ChatGPT to compounding one's productivity.
* **The "Unfair Advantage":** Humans remain superior at high-level strategy and system thinking. Altman suggests the biggest mistake young people make is "listening to old people" for career intuition, as the rate of change is unprecedented.

## India’s Strategic Role in AI Development
* **Market Significance:** India is already OpenAI’s second-largest market with 100 million ChatGPT users. Altman expects it to eventually become the company's largest market.
* **Building Energy:** India has the fastest-growing market for Codex (AI-assisted programming), largely driven by young developers.
* **Localized Innovation:** While OpenAI builds core frontier models, Altman believes Indian startups will be the ones to solve India-specific problems in healthcare, education, and tribal language access (e.g., the Aadibani tool).
* **Strategic Partnerships:** OpenAI is actively engaging with Indian institutions like IIT Delhi and corporations like the Tata Group to build sovereign AI models and compute infrastructure.

## Safety, Alignment, and Democratization
* **Three-Pillar Safety Framework:**
    * **Technical Alignment:** Developing methods to supervise systems that are smarter than their human creators.
    * **Security Architecture:** Creating new infrastructure to prevent agents from disclosing private data or executing "insane" commands (e.g., prompt injection).
    * **Resilience & Democratization:** Altman advocates for putting powerful AI in everyone’s hands rather than a "totalitarian" single-model control system. This assumes that a majority of good actors will keep bad actors in check.
* **The Human Signature:** In creative fields (art, architecture), value will continue to be derived from the "human imprint." AI-generated art with no human story currently trends toward zero value, whereas human-directed AI art remains highly valued.

## The Future of Work and Organizations
* **Zero-Person Companies:** Altman identifies the "zero-person" or "one-person" billion-dollar company as a massive underrated opportunity.
* **Job Transformation:** While some jobs will be "painful" to lose, Altman predicts a "player of games" style existence where society finds new ways to express creativity and gain status in a world where basic needs are met by automation.
* **Scientific Progress:** The automation of scientific discovery will be the single largest driver of economic value, potentially accelerating progress by 10x or 100x.

> "We've built up a lot of instincts and institutions to deal with a world of scarcity, but almost none of that applies well to a world of abundance." — **Sam Altman**

> "My willingness to fail allows me to succeed. Go be risk-taking. There's so much opportunity... take advantage of tools, curiosity, agency, and persistence." — **Vinod Khosla**

> "Young people always figure this out the best... I don’t even think you should trust me for having good intuition of the rate of change." — **Sam Altman**

briefings.title: George Noble on Gold’s Rise, Crypto Doubts & Tesla’s Struggles | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 47
briefings.tldr: George Noble argues for a massive rotation out of overextended technology and "failed" crypto assets into reflationary sectors like energy and precious metals, citing extreme fiscal debasement and a looming AI "spectacular bust."
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
George Noble argues for a massive rotation out of overextended technology and "failed" crypto assets into reflationary sectors like energy and precious metals, citing extreme fiscal debasement and a looming AI "spectacular bust."

## The Macro Case: Gold vs. Fiat Debasement
* **Fiat Currency Erosion:** George Noble argues that gold's rise isn't about the metal increasing in value, but about the dollar's decline. He illustrates this by comparing the US bond market denominated in gold (which looks "horrible") versus the dollar.
* **The "Hoover Dam" Analogy:** Noble suggests the US economy is at a "critical mass" regarding debt. While skeptics point to 40 years of failed "gold bug" predictions, Noble contends that bankruptcy happens "slowly and then suddenly," and current fiscal policies are no longer sustainable.
* **The Eisman Counter-Argument:** Steve Eisman remains skeptical of the "demise of the dollar" narrative, noting that the entire global financial system functions on Treasuries. Without a viable alternative (like Chinese bonds), the gold argument remains academic to him.
* **Central Bank Shifts:** Noble notes that foreign investors and central banks (particularly China) are increasingly less inclined to hold US debt, creating a "global Liz Truss moment" risk for the US bond market.

## Rotation and Energy Stocks
* **S&P 500 Concentration:** Energy currently accounts for only 3% of the S&P 500, while tech dominates at roughly 35%. Noble views this as an extreme imbalance ripe for reversal.
* **Outperformance Signals:** Noble points out that Schlumberger (SLB) has outperformed Microsoft by 100% over the last three months, signaling the "first inning" of a multi-year rotation.
* **Specific Energy Convictions:**
    * **Offshore Services:** Noble prefers service providers over commodity producers due to lower direct price volatility and higher upside. 
    * **Key Picks:** He highlights **Tidewater (TDW)** and **Schlumberger (SLB)**. He also mentions a preference for being long the Energy ETF (XLE) while shorting Technology (XLK).

## The Tesla and Opendoor "Fairy Tales"
* **Tesla’s Growth Reversal:** Noble characterizes Tesla as an auto company, not an AI firm. He notes that 2026 will likely be the third year of declining revenues, and earnings have crashed from a 2022 peak of $4.50/share toward a projected $1.50/share.
* **Robotaxi Valuation Disconnect:** Noble points out that Waymo, which is further ahead in autonomous tech, was recently valued at $125 billion. If Tesla's "robotaxi" business is valued similarly, the current $1.3 trillion market cap remains indefensible.
* **Cash Flow Warning:** Noble predicts Tesla may become cash-flow negative this year due to massive CapEx spending on robotics and AI despite collapsing auto sales.
* **Opendoor (OPEN) Accounting Criticism:** Noble labels Opendoor a "meme stock" for the "financial illiterati." 
    * **Revenue Inflation:** He criticizes the company for reporting the full sale price of a home as revenue rather than the actual margin, misleading investors on valuation multiples.

## Crypto Skepticism and the Gambling Shift
* **"Bitcoin is for Boomers":** Noble argues that Bitcoin has failed its test as "digital gold" because it correlates with risk assets rather than acting as an inflation hedge.
* **The Rise of Online Gambling:** Noble believes speculative liquidity is moving away from crypto and toward instant-gratification platforms like **FanDuel, DraftKings,** and **0DTE (zero days to expiration) options**.
* **Short Thesis on MicroStrategy (MSTR):** Both Noble and Eisman expressed significant skepticism toward MSTR, with Eisman explicitly stating he is short the stock, viewing it as a "carnival barker" play on Bitcoin.

## The AI Bubble: Parallels to .com
* **Capital Misallocation:** Citing research by Julian Garran, Noble suggests the capital misallocation in AI could be 17 times larger than the dot-com bubble.
* **Monetization Gap:** Noble notes that while AI tools are useful, the economics are flawed. Companies are currently underpricing services (charging $20/month for tools that cost $100+/month to run) to hook users, similar to early Uber/DoorDash models.
* **Performance Failure:** Noble cites a study where AI failed 98% of tasks sourced from Upwork, suggesting the technology is far from replacing human labor in a way that justifies current valuations.

> "Bitcoin is for old people... It’s like the Facebook of speculative assets." — George Noble

> "When growth is scarce, investors pay up for growth. When growth is plentiful, not so much... R is for rotation, not recession." — George Noble

> "It’s not what you don't know that's going to hurt you, it's what you think you know that ain't true." — George Noble (quoting Mark Twain)

> "I don't have the guts to short Tesla. I generally do not like to short anything that involves a cult." — Steve Eisman

briefings.title: LIVE: SecWar Speaks During a Nationwide Arsenal of Freedom Tour Stop at Sierra Space in Colorado
briefings.tldr: Secretary of War Pete Hegseth’s visit to Sierra Space marks a pivotal shift in the "Arsenal of Freedom" tour, emphasizing the integration of commercial space innovation into national defense to ensure American dominance in the contested domain of space.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Secretary of War Pete Hegseth’s visit to Sierra Space marks a pivotal shift in the "Arsenal of Freedom" tour, emphasizing the integration of commercial space innovation into national defense to ensure American dominance in the contested domain of space.

## The Arsenal of Freedom Initiative
*   **Strategic Re-industrialization:** Secretary Hegseth detailed the "Arsenal of Freedom" as a national effort to revitalize the American defense industrial base by bridging the gap between traditional military requirements and private sector agility.
*   **Bureaucratic Reform:** The initiative aims to strip away "legacy thinking" and procurement hurdles that have historically slowed down the deployment of new technologies.
    *   **Goal:** Moving at the "speed of relevance" to outpace global adversaries, particularly in the Indo-Pacific theater.
*   **Economic Impact:** The tour highlights the role of domestic manufacturing in Colorado as a cornerstone of both national security and local economic prosperity.

## Commercial Space Integration & Sierra Space
*   **Sierra Space Partnership:** Hegseth praised Sierra Space for its revolutionary platforms, specifically noting the importance of the **Dream Chaser** spaceplane for rapid, flexible logistics and reconnaissance.
*   **Infrastructure Beyond Earth:** Discussion centered on the development of commercial space stations, such as **Orbital Reef**, as critical nodes for future military research, manufacturing, and tactical operations.
*   **Cost-Effectiveness:** By leveraging commercial R&D, the Department of War aims to achieve superior technological capabilities at a fraction of the cost and time required by traditional government-only programs.

## Space as a Contested Warfighting Domain
*   **The "Ultimate High Ground":** Hegseth underscored that space is no longer a sanctuary but a primary theater of conflict where American interests are actively threatened by China and Russia.
*   **Deterrence Strategy:** The Department’s focus is on "resilient architecture"—ensuring that if one satellite or platform is neutralized, the entire network remains operational through rapid commercial launches and redundant systems.
*   **Technological Superiority:** Emphasis was placed on maintaining a qualitative edge in hypersonics, satellite defense, and secure communications.

## Workforce and the Future of Defense
*   **Talent Acquisition:** Hegseth highlighted the "patriotism of innovation," calling on the brightest engineers at Sierra Space to see their work as a direct contribution to the defense of the Republic.
*   **Skilled Labor Pipeline:** The briefing acknowledged the Colorado aerospace corridor as a vital ecosystem for technical talent, necessary for scaling the Arsenal of Freedom nationwide.
*   **Mission Readiness:** The Secretary reaffirmed that the Department of War’s primary focus is "lethality and winning," and that every commercial partnership must ultimately serve that end.

> "The original Arsenal of Democracy won World War II on the factory floors of the Midwest. The Arsenal of Freedom will be won in the clean rooms and launch pads of companies like Sierra Space. We are here to ensure that the next frontier remains an American frontier."
> — **Secretary Pete Hegseth**

> "We are done waiting decades for systems that are obsolete by the time they hit the field. If you can build it faster, better, and cheaper than a government bureaucracy, we want you in this fight."
> — **Secretary Pete Hegseth**

> "Freedom isn't free—it requires the high ground. And in the 21st century, there is no higher ground than the stars."
> — **Secretary Pete Hegseth**

briefings.tldr: Congressman James Comer and industry leaders emphasized the urgent need to modernize defense procurement by shifting away from slow, bureaucratic legacy systems toward rapid, software-defined hardware and competitive innovation to counter the technological advancements of adversaries like China.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Congressman James Comer and industry leaders emphasized the urgent need to modernize defense procurement by shifting away from slow, bureaucratic legacy systems toward rapid, software-defined hardware and competitive innovation to counter the technological advancements of adversaries like China.

## The Volatile Global Security Environment
*   **Pacing Challenges:** The U.S. currently faces an "unprecedented era of volatility," characterized by the rapid rise of China as a pacing threat and heightening Russian aggression in Ukraine.
*   **Regional Instability:** Ongoing conflicts in Israel and the potential for a Taiwan conflict represent significant risks to global stability and the fragility of international supply chains.
*   **Adversarial Speed:** China is investing heavily in AI, hypersonics, space, and autonomous systems. Unlike the U.S., they are moving with "speed and purpose," unconstrained by the same levels of institutional bureaucracy.

## Modernizing Defense Procurement
*   **Criticism of Legacy Systems:** The traditional defense procurement process is criticized for being slow, bureaucratic, and dominated by a few large companies that have utilized the same stagnant methods for decades.
*   **The Innovation Mandate:** To maintain a competitive edge, the Department of Defense (DOD) must embrace risk-taking and prioritize speed over bureaucratic tradition.
*   **Shifting the Reward Structure:** Congressional leaders aim to reform the system to reward performance and results rather than institutional longevity or political connections.

## The "Software-Defined" Defense Model
*   **Software-Defined Hardware:** Industry leaders argue that integrating advanced software with hardware is the only viable path to achieving the "mass and speed" required for modern warfare.
*   **Proactive Problem Solving:** New defense-tech firms are encouraged to develop innovative solutions based on battlefield needs rather than waiting for specific government requirements.
*   **Modular and Scalable Systems:** The future of defense relies on building systems that are modular, scalable, and cost-effective—ideally at a fraction of the cost of traditional defense contracts.

## Congressional Oversight and Legislative Goals
*   **Transparency and Efficiency:** As Chairman of the Oversight Committee, Rep. Comer emphasized the goal of ensuring that billions in defense spending are used effectively to provide the best possible equipment for troops.
*   **Lowering Barriers to Entry:** There is a bipartisan commitment to breaking down the barriers that prevent innovative startups and small businesses from entering the defense market.
*   **Partnership for Leadership:** Forging strong partnerships across the aisle and with private industry is viewed as essential to maintaining U.S. technological and military leadership.

> "China is investing heavily in AI, in hypersonics, in space, and in autonomous systems. They're not constrained by the same bureaucracy that we are. They're moving with speed and they're moving with purpose."
> — **Congressman James Comer**

> "At Anduril, we believe that software-defined hardware and mass and speed are really the only ways that we are going to prepare for this future and preserve the peace and promote human freedom."
> — **Anduril Representative**

> "We need to break down the barriers that prevent new and innovative companies from entering the defense market. We need to streamline the procurement process and we need to reward performance and results, not just longevity and political connections."
> — **Congressman James Comer**

briefings.title: Offense or Defense? Positioning Portfolios in Today's Market with Howard Marks and Alper Daglioglu

people.name: Alper Daglioglu
people.role: Head of Global Investment Strategies, Morgan Stanley

briefings.tldr: The current market is characterized by extreme optimism following a historic three-year bull run, signaling a critical need for investors to shift from aggressive growth toward defensive positioning and predictable outcomes.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR** 
The current market is characterized by extreme optimism following a historic three-year bull run, signaling a critical need for investors to shift from aggressive growth toward defensive positioning and predictable outcomes.

## Assessing the Current Market Cycle
* **Historic Performance:** The three-year period of 2023–2025 ranks as the 7th best three-year period for the S&P 500 in the last 100 years.
* **Sentiment Shift:** Optimism is currently "in the ascendancy." Howard Marks notes that when optimism rules, prices are high relative to intrinsic value, prospective returns are modest, and risk is elevated.
* **Strategic Adjustment:** Because the world remains highly unpredictable and certain 20th-century growth drivers (globalization, post-WWII recovery) are slowing, investors should prioritize defensiveness over sheer aggression.
* **Predictability vs. Maximization:** Investors face a fundamental tradeoff between maximizing returns and enhancing the reliability of those returns. Current conditions favor emphasizing "reliable outcomes."

## The Psychology of Risk and Contrarianism
* **Second-Level Thinking:** Successful investing requires the courage to be "uncomfortably idiosyncratic." Marks highlights that attractive valuations only appear during periods of "abject terror" (e.g., September 2008 or March 2020).
* **The Paradox of Risk:** The riskiest market environment is one where everyone believes there is no risk. Conversely, the safest time to buy is when the consensus believes risk is everywhere, as this sentiment drives prices to their floor.
* **Emotional Discipline:** Most human instincts—wanting to buy when things feel good and sell when things feel bad—are detrimental to wealth accumulation. To outperform, one must act as a contrarian, buying more when assets go "on sale."

## Overcoming Institutional and Behavioral Constraints
* **Volatility vs. Risk:** Marks argues that the investment industry wrongly equates volatility with risk. For long-term, well-funded investors, interim price fluctuations are a "part of life" and should not be avoided if they lead to higher terminal returns.
* **Agency Friction:** Institutional "agents" often prioritize career preservation over performance. This creates a bias toward avoiding losses that might lead to being fired, even at the cost of superior long-term gains.
* **The "Do Something" Bias:** Investors often focus on irrelevant short-term data, such as the exact month the Fed will stop raising rates. Marks asserts that "what really matters" is the long-term growth of company value and the ability of borrowers to repay debt.

## Evolving Asset Management Trends
* **Private Assets:** The shift toward private markets offers a "liquidity trade-off." While these assets lack daily mark-to-market pricing (reducing perceived volatility), they require specialized manager skill to navigate the lack of reference prices.
* **Concentrated Partnerships:** Global allocators are trending toward fewer, deeper relationships with General Partners (GPs). These strategic partnerships aim to treat the manager as an extension of the investor’s team to solve complex liability and liquidity needs over 5–10 year horizons.
* **Artificial Intelligence:** While AI will undoubtedly change the world, Marks warns that the "how, when, and who benefits" remains uncertain. Superior investing in this space will rely on personal judgment rather than "machinable" formulas.

> "The riskiest thing in the world is the belief that there's no risk. So one of the safest things in the world is the belief that risk is everywhere, because it puts prices so low that risk is minimal." — **Howard Marks**

> "It’s nothing short of an oxymoron to say, 'this is a bargain-priced security that everybody loves.' When everybody loves something, it’s unlikely that it’ll be on the bargain counter." — **Howard Marks**

> "Buffett says, 'I’d rather have a lumpy 15% return than a smooth 12.' And I would say to people, if you’d rather have a smooth 12 than a lumpy 15, you have to ask yourself what’s going on." — **Howard Marks**

briefings.title: Sam Altman at India AI Summit: 'Superintelligence is only a couple of years away' | Tech Today
briefings.tldr: India is positioning itself as the global "nerve center" for AI through a $100B+ mission focused on inclusivity and ethical governance, while OpenAI CEO Sam Altman predicts the emergence of early superintelligence by 2028.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
India is positioning itself as the global "nerve center" for AI through a $100B+ mission focused on inclusivity and ethical governance, while OpenAI CEO Sam Altman predicts the emergence of early superintelligence by 2028.

## India’s Strategic AI Vision and Governance
* **Global Leadership:** The India AI Impact Summit 2026 signals India’s shift from a technology consumer to a primary agenda-setter for global AI governance and ethics.
* **Investment and Infrastructure:** The "India AI Mission" has secured over $100 billion in potential investment commitments, supported by a shared global framework for safe AI.
* **Inclusivity Philosophy:** The summit's theme, *"Sarvajan hitay, sarvajan sukhay"* (Welfare for all, happiness of all), emphasizes making AI tools open-source and accessible to ensure the technology benefits the masses rather than a select few.
* **US-India Partnership:** Tech leaders highlighted a "full-stack commitment" between the US and India, involving trade agreements, skilling, and infrastructure to build a robust long-term tech partnership.

## The Road to Superintelligence and Economic Shift
* **2028 Milestone:** Sam Altman projected that the world is only a few years away from "true superintelligence," suggesting that by the end of 2028, more intellectual capacity could reside within data centers than outside of them.
* **Cost Reduction:** Automated supply chains and AI-driven robotics are expected to significantly lower the cost of physical goods and services, such as healthcare and education.
* **Labor Disruption:** Altman warned that as AI assumes more roles within the economy, global society will face a critical test regarding job displacement and the choice between empowering the workforce or concentrating power.

## Consumer Hardware and Physical AI
* **Affordable Wearables:** Jio showcased smart glasses designed specifically for the Indian market.
    * **Inclusivity:** Features multi-lingual AI support to assist non-English speakers, such as farmers identifying plant diseases in their native dialects.
    * **Pricing:** Targeted at approximately half the cost of international competitors like Meta Ray-Bans (est. ₹20,000 vs ₹40,000).
* **Autonomous Logistics:** Startups demonstrated end-to-end delivery ecosystems where drones deliver packages to smart mailboxes, and robots handle the "last mile" to the customer’s door.
    * **Social Impact:** This aims to improve the "quality of life" for delivery workers and enhance security in gated communities.
* **Humanoid Robotics:** Qualcomm showcased the Booster K1 robot, which uses spatial technology and camera systems to interact with humans through context-aware gestures like "Namaste."

## Industrial and Creative Applications
* **Textile Innovation:** Tata showcased AI-assisted weaving for Kanchipuram sarees.
    * **Efficiency:** AI reduces the design-to-weave process from weeks to just one or two days.
    * **LED Assistance:** A technological "standing assistant" guides weavers on color and direction, reducing pressure during complex, multi-day projects.
* **Creative Design:** IDEA Jewellery uses fine-tuned AI models to convert user sketches into unique 3D-modeled gold and silver pieces, ensuring designs are non-replicable.
* **Educational Robotics:** Gujarat-based startup STEMbotix is deploying low-cost (starting at ₹3,000) robotics kits to over 5,000 rural schools to train the next generation in coding and semiconductor fundamentals.

## Notable Quotes

> "On our current trajectory, we believe we may be only a couple of years away from early versions of true superintelligence. If we are right, by the end of 2028, more of the world's intellectual capacity could reside inside of data centers than outside of them." 
— **Sam Altman**, CEO, OpenAI

> "AI jaisi takniki tabhi duniya ke liye labhkari hogi jab use share kiya jayega... (AI technology will only be beneficial to the world when it is shared... when codes are open, our millions of young minds can make them better and safer.)" 
— **Narendra Modi**, Prime Minister of India (quoted during inaugural address)

> "The limit to how far this cost reduction [of physical goods] can go may only be government policy. But the other side of this coin is that current jobs are going to get disrupted as AI can do more and more of the things that drive our economy today." 
— **Sam Altman**, CEO, OpenAI

> "In a typical group housing society in India, there are 30 to 40 delivery boys in and out... It’s a massive deficit in security. We are trying to bring this orchestration system so that people can be doing more meaningful work and the dull and dusty can be done by robots." 
— **Ritukar**, Co-founder of a logistics robotics startup

briefings.title: Thin Is In | Stratechery by Ben Thompson
briefings.tldr: The rise of generative AI is driving a shift back to "thin client" computing where local hardware matters less than cloud connectivity, a transition being accelerated by an AI-driven global memory shortage that makes local devices more expensive and less essential.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
The rise of generative AI is driving a shift back to "thin client" computing where local hardware matters less than cloud connectivity, a transition being accelerated by an AI-driven global memory shortage that makes local devices more expensive and less essential.

## The Resurgence of the Thin Client Paradigm
* **Historical Context:** Computing has swung between "thin clients" (terminals connected to mainframes) and "thick clients" (PCs where compute and I/O are local). While mobile and SaaS were hybrids, they remained essentially thick because the user interface (UI) and interaction were processed locally.
* **AI as the Great Leveler:** AI shifts the focus from local processing power to connectivity.
    * **Minimalist UI:** In a chat-based interface, the only local requirements are a text field and a submit button; the actual "work" happens entirely in a remote data center.
    * **Device Agnosticism:** The quality of an AI experience is independent of whether the user is on a high-end PC, a cheap smartphone, or an earpiece.
* **The Death of Vertical Software Moats:** **Nicolas Bustamante** notes that for many software companies, the UI *was* the value.
    * When natural language replaces complex workflows, years of "muscle memory" and high switching costs for expensive software seats evaporate.

## From User Interface to Agentic Outcomes
* **Invisible Computing:** The next wave of AI—agents—aims to move beyond chat to accomplishing specific tasks. 
    * This represents the extreme of the thin client: the user doesn't need local compute to perform work; the AI on the server handles everything between the request and the result.
* **The Compute/Memory Threshold:** Agentic workflows currently struggle with complex edge cases, but this is changing as chips improve and context windows expand.
* **Economic Centralization:** High-performance AI is increasingly centralized in data centers for three reasons:
    * **Performance:** Workloads flow to the best available compute.
    * **Memory:** Large models require massive amounts of memory for context, which is more available in the cloud.
    * **Utilization:** Sharing the massive upfront costs of AI hardware across millions of users is more economical than individual local ownership.

## The Global Memory "Crowd-Out"
* **Supply Chain Crisis:** AI's demand for High-Bandwidth Memory (HBM) is siphoning resources away from traditional consumer electronics.
    * **Gaming Delays:** Sony is reportedly considering delaying the next PlayStation (PS6) to 2028 or 2029 due to memory shortages.
    * **Pricing Pressure:** Nintendo may raise the price of the Switch 2, and Chinese smartphone makers like Xiaomi and Oppo are trimming shipment targets due to rising component costs.
* **The Nvidia Shift:** **Ben Thompson** highlights that even at the Consumer Electronics Show (CES), Nvidia’s focus has shifted from gaming GPUs to AI systems and self-driving platforms.
* **Contract Volatility:** Major suppliers like Samsung are moving from annual memory contracts to quarterly reviews to capture rapidly escalating prices.

## The Diminishing Returns of Local Hardware
* **The Plateau of "Good Enough":** Thick clients like PCs, phones, and consoles have reached a point of diminishing returns.
    * Current hardware is already sufficient for most legacy tasks, making the high cost of upgrading to even "thicker" local AI hardware unappealing for many.
* **The Local Inference Barrier:** While local AI (running models on your own device) is "free" in terms of electricity, it is currently limited by model size and context window constraints. 
* **Path Dependency:** By the time local hardware catches up to current AI needs, most user workflows will have already migrated to cloud-based architectures, making a return to thick-client dominance unlikely.

> "When the interface is a natural language conversation, years of muscle memory become worthless. The switching cost that justified the twenty-five thousand dollars per seat per year dissolves. For many vertical software companies, the interface was most of the value... That’s over." — **Nicolas Bustamante**

> "A big story over the last few months has been the dramatically escalating cost of memory as the major memory manufacturers shift their focus to high-bandwidth memory for AI chips in particular. What that means is that everything else is going to get a lot more expensive." — **Ben Thompson**

> "Thick clients—of which consoles like the PS5 are the ultimate example—have long since reached the point of diminishing returns when it comes to hardware improvements... what we already have is already more than sufficient for almost any task we want to do." — **Ben Thompson**

briefings.title: Why one CEO sets ‘non -goals’ - and what ultramarathons taught him about focus and mental toughness
briefings.tldr: Nicholas Thompson, CEO of The Atlantic, applies the discipline of ultramarathon running to leadership, advocating for the use of "non-goals" to sharpen organizational focus and emphasizing that consistent effort—rather than raw talent or time—is the key to breaking through mental barriers and managing digital disruption.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR:** Nicholas Thompson, CEO of *The Atlantic*, applies the discipline of ultramarathon running to leadership, advocating for the use of "non-goals" to sharpen organizational focus and emphasizing that consistent effort—rather than raw talent or time—is the key to breaking through mental barriers and managing digital disruption.

## The "Non-Goal" Strategy and Effective Prioritization
Thompson utilizes a specific framework to manage energy and time in high-pressure environments:

*   **Defining "Non-Goals":** A non-goal is a task that is objectively valuable but for which there is currently no time. 
    *   **Strategic Benchmarking:** By explicitly labeling something a "non-goal," a leader ensures that every active project is demonstrably more valuable than that omitted task.
    *   **Example:** For *The Atlantic*, developing a comprehensive video strategy is currently a non-goal, allowing resources to stay focused on higher-yield subscription and advertising engines.
*   **The Trello Methodology:** Thompson manages his daily workflow using three distinct boards:
    *   **The Top Five:** The most critical priorities for the day.
    *   **The Next Three:** Tasks to tackle next, or specific time-blocks (e.g., "20 minutes on X").
    *   **Aspirational/General:** Long-term projects and general goals.
*   **Energy Management vs. Time Management:** Borrowing from marathon training, leaders should only "run hard" two or three times a week. 
    *   **Pacing:** Avoid "frying" yourself early in the week (e.g., at events like Davos) to ensure peak performance for high-stakes panels or meetings later.

## Leadership Lessons from Ultramarathoning
Thompson’s book, *The Running Ground*, explores how physical discipline translates into professional resilience:

*   **Breaking Mental Limits:** Pain is often a mental process of "fear"—the brain’s attempt to protect the body from perceived limits. 
    *   **Barrier Cracking:** Once Thompson broke the mental block of a 2:40 marathon, he quickly improved to a 2:29. Leaders must similarly identify where "mental blocks" are stalling organizational speed.
*   **The Principle of Consistent Effort:** Growth is a byproduct of steady, daily work. 
    *   **Overcoming Procrastination:** When faced with an "impossible" six-month project, Thompson’s advice is to "just start" rather than complaining about the timeline.
*   **Restraint and "Organizational Fatigue":** A runner must know the difference between fatigue and injury. 
    *   **Calibrating Pressure:** Leaders must sense how much pressure their teams can handle. Instead of demanding a 100% increase in speed, aim to motivate people to the top of their current abilities while building their "capacity" for more later.
*   **Intentional Reflection:** Thompson runs without music to maintain a "meditative state" and stay in touch with his body’s signals. He argues that leaders need similar "imaginative spaces" to process thoughts without digital distraction.

## Navigating Digital Transformation and the AI Frontier
As the leader of a 169-year-old publication, Thompson focuses on modernizing *The Atlantic*’s business model:

*   **The OpenAI Partnership:** Thompson negotiated a deal with OpenAI to compensate the publication for its data and collaborate on search experiences.
    *   **Strategy:** While some media companies sued, Thompson sought a model that respects journalism while driving traffic in a post-search world.
*   **The Democratization of AI:** A major concern is whether AI will be controlled by five giant companies or become "democratized" through open-source and sovereign models.
    *   **The Vertical vs. Horizontal Race:** Thompson supports the "horizontal race," where independent organizations build new architectures and value systems that aren't purely dependent on massive "scaling laws" (billions in compute/money).
*   **AI as a "Giant Magnet":** Thompson views AI as a tool for journalists to find "needles in haystacks," assisting with research, engineering tickets, and customer service rather than replacing core editorial judgment.

## Dealing with Imperfect Mentors and Difficult People
Drawing from his relationship with his father, Scott Thompson, Nicholas highlights the importance of navigating complex relationships:

*   **Accepting Imperfection:** Mentors are rarely "gleaming people on pedestals." Thompson learned to work through chaos and personal failings to maintain a productive relationship.
*   **Workplace Adaptability:** Being able to tolerate and extract the best from difficult people is a vital leadership skill. Thompson suggests identifying what a boss or report *can* do well, rather than focusing solely on their shortcomings.

***

**Notable Quotes**

> "I use a principle called non-goals, which is: what is a thing that is valuable that I do not have time for? ... Everything I do has to be more valuable than that. It's a way to structure your day so that you actually aren't spending time on stuff that's valuable, scattered, [but] not useful." — **Nicholas Thompson**

> "One of the most interesting things I learned about running is that pain is not necessarily a physical process... It's your body being afraid of what's happening. Once you can crack these barriers in your mind, you can go a lot faster." — **Nicholas Thompson**

> "Don't complain about how you can't get it done, just start! ... If you worry about not having the time, you definitely won't get it done." — **Nicholas Thompson**

> "I think that the benefits of AI will start to match the investments... but there might be a crash. AI is going to disrupt my business really soon in ways that no one in it understands." — **Nicholas Thompson**
